summary: A skeleton tower on the west end of Île de Caraquet, New Brunswick, on Chaleur Bay. The light was first shown in 1870; the present tower dates from the 1950s, and the island is reached only by boat.

structures.note: Present skeletal tower, put up around the 1950s to replace the original station (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). Skeleton tower with a red enclosed top and white slatwork daymark (CCG).

Original combined lighthouse and dwelling, erected 1870 by Daly and Carter of Miramichi: a one-and-a-half-storey house with a square tower at one end of its pitched roof. Replaced around the 1950s. The sources do not say what became of it.

staffing.note: Keepers are named to at least 1953 (LighthouseFriends). The sources do not say when keeping ended.

access.note: Reached only by boat. The site is open; the tower is closed (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends).

visit.note: A distant view can be had from the mainland, but the light is best seen by boat (LighthouseFriends). Tower closed.

events.note: Combined lighthouse and dwelling erected by Daly and Carter of Miramichi at a cost of $548.
Fixed white light first exhibited 26 August 1870. Rowlett gives the station as established 1870.
Keeper's son Archibald Kerr drowned on 14 October 1872 about the same place where his father later drowned.
Keeper Thomas Kerr drowned on 13 June 1873 when his small flat upset on the crossing from the mainland.
Keeper Narcisse Porlier drowned just off the island in October 1876 when a gale capsized his boat.
Illuminating apparatus changed to a dioptric light. A storeroom and a well were built the same year.
Gervais Lantaigne appointed 16 June 1888 (the Marine keeper table, read by column position).
Original lighthouse replaced by the present skeletal tower, around the 1950s.
Name officially changed to Île de Caraquet (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Thomas Kerr
keepers.note: Appointed at an annual salary of $200. Drowned 13 June 1873 on the crossing from the mainland, while returning from the mainland after mailing returns and papers connected with the light (Union Advocate, as transcribed on Find a Grave). Spelled KERR in the transcriptions.

keepers.name: Mary Kerr
keepers.note: Keeper Kerr's wife. Took over responsibility for the light for the rest of the 1873 shipping season (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Narcisse Porlier
keepers.note: Described by Inspector Mitchell in 1874 as a very efficient officer. Drowned off the island in October 1876 when a gale capsized his boat (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Louis Porlier
keepers.note: Appointed in late October 1876 in place of his father. His widowed mother appears to have cared for the light while he was listed as the official keeper (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Gervais Lantaigne
keepers.note: Named against Caraquet Island in the 1903 keeper list (printed p. 215) and appointed 16 June 1888 in the 1904 table (printed p. 159); both checked on the page images. LighthouseFriends gives 1888 to 1924.

keepers.name: André V. Gionet
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends gives an end date of 1947 and no start date.

corrections.why: The record's position comes from OpenStreetMap. The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights (entry 1322, H1588) gives 47 49 21.2 N, 064 54 16.0 W, which LighthouseFriends also gives. The two points are about 45 m apart. A reviewer should confirm.
The 20.1 m tower is the skeletal tower that replaced the 1870 station around the 1950s (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). The 1870 building is not the present tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard list (the official source) gives Fl W 6s with a focal height of 22.3 m and a range of 9 nm, and the record keeps that. Rowlett's directory gives a white flash every 4 seconds, and the OpenStreetMap value in the record is Fl W 4s. No source explains the change, so the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Keepers from 1870 to 1882 and the 1870s deaths rest on LighthouseFriends, which cites Annual Reports of the Department of Marine and an unnamed newspaper account. The Marine reports for those years are not in the local corpus (it starts in 1900). The 1873 drowning and its search are confirmed only by the Find a Grave transcriptions of the Union Advocate and the Daily Telegraph (second-hand; the newspapers themselves were not read; the Daily Telegraph transcription (23 June 1873) says the body was not yet found, and the Union Advocate (9 July 1873) reports that a coroner viewed it on 27 June; the two are in sequence, and the story states both). The 1872 date for Archibald Kerr rests on the same transcription. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts paraphrased, quotations kept short. Keeper names from the Marine tables were checked on the page images: Lantaigne (1903 keeper list, printed p. 215, scan 228; 1904 appointment 16 June 1888, printed p. 159, scan 172). The printed pages were read from the page images on 2026-10-28 (printed p. 215 for the 1903 list, printed p. 159 for the 1904 table). The page image was checked: the Caraquet Island row sits against Lantaigne's name in the 1903 list, and the 16 June 1888 appointment sits in the 1904 table. Disagreement: the flash is Fl W 6s in the Coast Guard list and every 4 s in Rowlett; the story gives both; the record keeps the Coast Guard value. Position: the record's OpenStreetMap point is about 45 m from the Coast Guard point (corrections). Not checked: the Coast Guard entry for the 1870 tower (not in the list). LighthouseFriends' 2009 renaming (Hédard Albert, minister) is not confirmed in any second source; the Coast Guard list uses Île de Caraquet. The Caraquet range lights (1903 onward, Lower Caraquet) are separate stations and are not in this story. Not used: Wikipedia (fr, 'Île de Caraquet'; a lead only), the New Brunswick Provincial Archives (archives.gnb.ca, blocked in DESIGN section 2), the Nature Connexion copy of LighthouseFriends, and the Facebook group posts. Newspapers were not searched through newspapers.py: Chronicling America does not hold New Brunswick papers. Photos: none found with a clear licence. Keeper André V. Gionet has no start date in any source. Living people: the Gionets and Amedee Robert are named only as LighthouseFriends names them (1925 to 1953), with no personal detail.
